scopeMarkdown:
Make `rayx` a versioned, released product: every merged release PR publishes a GitHub Release of `rayx-ui/RayX.CLI` with the binaries of all six targets, checksums, attestations and the shell/PowerShell installers, and those installers fully install or update `rayx` (download, verify, `~/.rayx/bin`, PATH, install receipt) so `rayx self update` works afterwards. The first release is **v1.0.0**.

## In scope

- **Release builds (cargo-dist):** upgrade dist to 0.33.0 and regenerate `release.yml`; install into `~/.rayx/bin` (`$RAYX_HOME/bin` first); build `aarch64-pc-windows-msvc` on a hosted Windows x64 runner instead of the cargo-xwin container; GitHub artifact attestations; every pull request builds and uploads all six targets (`pr-run-mode = "upload"`) so the release build is proven before any tag.
- **Release automation (release-plz):** a release PR on `main` with the version bump and a `CHANGELOG.md` generated from Conventional Commits; merging it tags `vX.Y.Z` with the fine-grained PAT secret `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN`, which starts the dist workflow. dist, not release-plz, creates the GitHub Release.
- **Version 1.0.0** in `Cargo.toml` and the first `CHANGELOG.md` section.
- **Dependency rule relaxation:** crates.io, public git repositories pinned to a `rev` (Gpux is public, Apache-2.0) and a reasoned, upstream-linked `[patch]` are allowed; `path` dependencies on sibling checkouts and any dependency on RayX or another private repository stay forbidden. `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` and the package-layout test follow.
- **WSL:** `rayx setup --wsl` installs the Linux `rayx` with the release's versioned installer, so it lives in `~/.rayx/bin` with a receipt and `rayx self update` works inside WSL.
- **Docs:** README install section (latest and pinned one-liners, install location, update, attestation check, manual macOS download note) and `docs/releasing.md` (how a release happens, the token and its rotation, the by-hand fallback).
- **First release and consumers:** publish v1.0.0, verify installs on real hosts, and switch RayX CI from `cargo install --git --rev` to the pinned v1.0.0 installer (paired RayX commit).

## Out of scope

- macOS signing and notarization (deferred by the owner until iOS work needs an Apple Developer account), Windows code signing.
- winget, Scoop, Homebrew, MSI, npm installers; crates.io publishing (`publish = false` stays).
- A `rayx self update --version` pin/rollback flag; changes to `src/update.rs` behaviour (its install URLs stay valid).
- A GitHub App token (the owner chose a fine-grained PAT).
- Dropping axoupdater or its TLS stack, unless the Windows ARM64 fallback in the design fails and the owner decides it.

## Owner decisions (2026-10-14)

- Install location `~/.rayx/bin`; release-plz with a fine-grained PAT named `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN`; start at 1.0.0; WSL installer switch and RayX CI change in this epic; relax the dependency rule (Gpux is public); signing deferred.

## Owner prerequisites

- Before the first release (sprint s5): create the fine-grained PAT (resource owner `rayx-ui`, only `RayX.CLI`, Contents and Pull requests read/write) and store it as the repository secret `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN`.
- Pushing branches, opening and merging pull requests in `rayx-ui/RayX.CLI` and `rayx-ui/RayX` are outward-facing actions the implementer confirms with the owner each time.
constraintsMarkdown:
- `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` rules hold: every external program through `host::Runner`, `rayx` never reads, stores or forwards a password or token (the PAT exists only as a CI secret), Conventional Commits with scopes and no co-author lines.
- The generated `release.yml` is changed only through `dist-workspace.toml` and `dist generate`; no `allow-dirty`.
- The asset names and URL layout consumers already use stay valid: `releases/latest/download/rayx-cli-installer.{sh,ps1}`, `releases/download/v<version>/rayx-cli-<triple>.<ext>`.
- Tests are new feature groups in `tests/<feature>.rs`; while iterating run only the touched group.

requirements.title: Release builds for all six targets
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: cargo-dist builds, packages and publishes `rayx` for every target on GitHub-hosted runners.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
A pull-request run of the Release workflow on `rayx-ui/RayX.CLI` builds all six targets on GitHub-hosted runners and uploads their archives (`.tar.xz` for macOS/Linux, `.zip` for Windows), `.sha256` files, both installers and the dist manifest as workflow artifacts. The `aarch64-pc-windows-msvc` archive holds an ARM64 `rayx.exe` (checked with `file` or the PE machine field); the musl archives hold static binaries.

If the Windows ARM64 build fails on `windows-2022`, the failure log is recorded and the design's fallback order applies (build setup for `clang-cl`, then an axoasset TLS-backend change with a temporary pinned `[patch]`); the criterion passes only when all six build.

Verified by the green run's URL and the downloaded artifacts.

requirements.title: Release automation with release-plz
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Conventional Commits drive the version and changelog; merging a release PR publishes the release.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`Cargo.toml` (and `Cargo.lock`) carry version `1.0.0`, so `rayx --version` prints `rayx 1.0.0`. `CHANGELOG.md` exists with a `## [1.0.0]` section that summarizes the first release (the commands `setup`, `doctor`, `wsl`, `self update`, `app`, `fmt`, the six targets and the installers) rather than every historical commit.

As a lasting invariant, the test asserts that `CHANGELOG.md` has a section for the version in `Cargo.toml` and that the version is at least 1.0.0, so later release PRs keep both in step.

Verified by the new group `tests/release_automation.rs`.

requirements.title: Dependency sources anyone can fetch
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: The repository may depend on public code beyond crates.io while staying buildable from a clean clone on any machine.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` (kept identical) state the new rule: dependencies must be fetchable by anyone who clones the public repository, on any machine and CI runner: crates.io, public git repositories pinned to a `rev` (Gpux included), and `[patch]` for a recorded reason with a comment linking the upstream issue or PR, removed once upstream releases it; no `path` dependency on a sibling checkout and no dependency on RayX or any other private repository. The sentence calling Gpux a private sibling is corrected (Gpux is public under Apache-2.0; RayX is private).

Verified by review.

requirements.title: The Linux rayx in WSL comes from the release installer
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: `rayx setup --wsl` installs the same version inside the distribution the way users install it, so it can update itself there.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
After v1.0.0 is published, on the owner's Windows PC: `rayx setup --wsl` (from a v1.0.0 Windows `rayx`) installs `rayx 1.0.0` into `~/.rayx/bin` of `Ubuntu-24.04`, a new WSL shell finds `rayx` on PATH, and `rayx self update --check` inside WSL reports it up to date instead of the no-receipt message.

Verified by the owner's run, recorded in `docs/manual-verification.md`.

requirements.title: Install documentation
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: The README tells a user exactly how to install, pin, update and verify `rayx`.

requirements.title: The first release and its consumers
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: v1.0.0 is published through the new flow, installs on real hosts, and RayX uses it.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
With `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` in place and the epic merged to `main`, release-plz opens (or the first run directly performs) the v1.0.0 release; `ci.yml` runs on the release PR; merging it pushes the tag `v1.0.0`, and the Release workflow publishes the GitHub Release `v1.0.0` (not a prerelease, marked Latest) with the six archives, their `.sha256` files, `rayx-cli-installer.sh`, `rayx-cli-installer.ps1` and notes taken from the `CHANGELOG.md` section. `gh attestation verify` succeeds for at least the Windows x64 and macOS ARM64 archives.

If release-plz cannot produce the first tag from an untagged history, the documented by-hand fallback cuts `v1.0.0` and release-plz takes over from that tag; the deviation is recorded.

Verified by `gh release view v1.0.0 --json` output and the workflow run URLs.

From the `releases/latest` one-liners, on a host without `rayx`: Windows x64 (owner's PC) and macOS ARM64 (this Mac), plus Linux x64 (WSL or a container): `rayx` lands in `~/.rayx/bin`, a new shell finds it on PATH, `rayx --version` prints `rayx 1.0.0`, `rayx self update --check` reports up to date, and running the installer again reinstalls in place without error. A `rayx` previously built from source or with `cargo install` elsewhere on PATH is reported, not silently shadowed (note which one the shell resolves).

Verified by the owner's runs, recorded in `docs/manual-verification.md` (replacing "Not verifiable before a release").

In `rayx-ui/RayX` (paired commit): `.github/workflows/pr-test.yml` replaces `RAYX_CLI_REV` and both `cargo install --git ... --rev` steps with `RAYX_CLI_VERSION: 1.0.0` and the installer of that version (`releases/download/v${RAYX_CLI_VERSION}/rayx-cli-installer.sh | sh`), with `~/.rayx/bin` on `GITHUB_PATH` for later steps (added explicitly unless the installer already does it); the comment about the pinned commit is updated. `docs/src/rayx.md` drops the `--branch feature/initial-setup` source install for the release one-liners and the pinned form. RayX's memory decision text about `RAYX_CLI_REV` is synced to the release pin. A RayX pull-request run of both jobs is green with the release-installed `rayx`.

Verified by the RayX CI run URL.
